name: Jin Xiaotang
current_role: Director and General Manager, Shanghai Beite Technology Group (北特科技, SSE: 603009)
profile: Jin Xiaotang (靳晓堂) is the son of Beite founder and controlling shareholder Jin Kun, acts in concert with him, and holds ~8% of the Shanghai-listed auto-parts maker (steering rack bars, shock-absorber rods, A/C compressors, aluminium parts). He has been a director and general manager since January 2019; in 2025 the company renamed itself Shanghai Beite Technology Group.
interesting_fact: Beite is pivoting into humanoid robotics: in 2024 it set up Jiangsu Beite Robot Technology to make planetary roller screws, planning ~2.6m sets/yr in Kunshan plus a Thailand base, an RMB 1.85bn bet.
notes: Wealth shared with father Jin Kun (chairman, ~31.6%). Low public profile; route via company board secretary Liu Gongyou (IR email above). Role per 2024 acquisition report; check latest SSE filings to confirm GM title.

name: Lu Cheng
profile: Listed by Hurun (China lists 2008-2026, Global 2026) as 卢诚 with wealth from Nongfu Spring, the Hangzhou bottled-water and beverage group controlled by Zhong Shanshan. No public filing, company bio or press profile linking a person named 卢诚 to Nongfu Spring or its parent Yangshengtang could be found; he is not among the Nongfu Spring directors or senior management named in HKEX disclosures.
notes: Identity unverified: likely an early/indirect Nongfu Spring shareholder or Yangshengtang-linked investor with no public profile. Searches in Chinese and English (HKEX exec lists, Nongfu/Yangshengtang press) returned nothing. Do not approach without further verification.

name: Gail Jones
current_role: Former co-founder, managing director and acting CEO of UKFast (Manchester hosting/cloud provider); no current public operating role identified
profile: Gail Jones co-founded Manchester web-hosting firm UKFast in 1999 with her husband Lawrence Jones and grew it into one of the UK's largest independent hosting/cloud providers with its own data-centre campus (UKFast Campus, Trafford). She became MD in 2017 and led the firm after Lawrence stepped down in 2019; the family sold its remaining interest to Inflexion in 2020, and UKFast was merged into ANS.
interesting_fact: UKFast ran its own Manchester data-centre estate (MaNOC) and in 2017 split its leadership into two MD roles, with co-founder Gail Jones taking the managing director post to drive cloud growth.
notes: Left UKFast in 2020 (FT). Very low public profile since. Sensitive: husband Lawrence Jones was convicted in 2023 of rape/sexual offences; avoid referencing him in outreach. Reported prior board roles at Tech Manchester and Manchester Foundation Trust Charity (unverified on primary sources). No published contact found.

name: Shao Xionghui
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Zhaomin New Material Technology (肇民科技, SZSE: 301000)
profile: Shao Xionghui (邵雄辉, b. 1976) controls Shanghai Zhaomin (Hurun English 'Hajime'), a ChiNext-listed maker of precision engineering-plastic parts for auto powertrain, thermal-management and appliance systems. He joined its Japanese-invested predecessor Zhaomin Precision Plastics in 2003, rose to general manager, took over the business in 2012 and has been chairman and GM since 2019; re-elected June 2025.
interesting_fact: He started out in tourism, not manufacturing: from 1996 to 2003 he worked in the Japan department of Hunan Huatian International Travel Service, rising to deputy head, before moving into the Japanese-founded plastics firm he would later own.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he spent seven years (1996-2003) at Hunan Huatian International Travel Service's Japan department, going from staff member to deputy department head; his Japan background carried into Zhaomin Precision Plastics (Shanghai), where he worked his way up from manufacturing-department head.
notes: Board secretary is Xiao Jun (肖俊). Low media profile; best route is the company securities office email. Holds ~18m shares directly plus ~90m via Shanghai Jizhao and other vehicles.

name: Han Hongwei
current_role: Founder/controller of Hywin Wealth (海银财富) and chairman of China Guijiu Group (中国贵酒集团); reportedly in police custody since Sept 2024
profile: Han Hongwei (韩宏伟) built Shanghai-based Hywin Wealth, a third-party wealth manager whose holding company listed on Nasdaq, and China Guijiu Group, a baijiu business that controlled Shanghai-listed Yanshi/Shanghai Guijiu (600696), run by his son Han Xiao. In Sept 2024 Shanghai police opened an illegal-fundraising case against Hywin Wealth and took several suspects, including Han Xiao, into criminal custody; media reported Han Hongwei was among those taken.
interesting_fact: A self-described army veteran, he said in 2020 that he aimed to use Guijiu's 'military liquor' range to help 30,000 retired servicemen start their own businesses.
notes: NOT SUITABLE FOR OUTREACH: Hywin Wealth is under criminal investigation for illegal fundraising (~RMB 70bn of investor products halted); son Han Xiao detained; Shanghai Guijiu (600696) was ordered delisted in 2026. Reports say Han Hongwei was taken away by police in Sept 2024 (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2024-09-11/3554578.html). No contacts recorded.

name: Liu Shaosheng
current_role: Minority shareholder in the Yihua (宜华) group of Shantou, Guangdong; no current executive role found
profile: Liu Shaosheng (刘绍生) appeared on Hurun China lists 2005-2010 alongside Liu Shaoxi (刘绍喜), founder of the Shantou-based Yihua Group (wood furniture/flooring via Yihua Lifestyle, property, later healthcare). Exchange filings list him as a 7% shareholder of a Yihua holding entity in which Liu Shaoxi held 56%. Little else about him is public.
interesting_fact: Yihua began as a Chenghai township wood-products business and grew into one of China's biggest solid-wood furniture exporters, with group assets once reported at RMB 85bn.
notes: Not recommended: the Yihua group fell into a debt crisis from 2019; Yihua Lifestyle was delisted in 2021 and Liu Shaoxi was placed under CSRC investigation for alleged market manipulation (2023). Liu Shaosheng's relationship to Liu Shaoxi (likely brother, not confirmed) and current status are unverified. No public contacts.

name: Lam Shun Chiu
current_role: Chairman and CEO, C-MER Medical Holdings (formerly C-MER Eye Care Holdings, HKEX: 3309)
profile: Dr Dennis Lam Shun-chiu (林顺潮) is a Hong Kong ophthalmologist (HKU MBBS 1984) who chaired the Chinese University of Hong Kong's ophthalmology department 1998-2008, then founded C-MER in 2012. It listed in Hong Kong in 2018 and now runs about 70 eye and medical facilities across Hong Kong and mainland China (incl. Shenzhen C-MER Dennis Lam Eye Hospital). He is also a long-serving NPC deputy.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he operated on a six-year-old Shanxi boy whose eyes had been gouged out, a case that made his newly opened Shenzhen eye hospital nationally famous.
deep_cut_fact: His Project Vision Charitable Foundation (founded 2004) follows a 'teach people to fish' model: it has trained 160+ cataract surgeons, set up 32 'poverty-alleviation ophthalmic centres' in China and done 200,000+ cataract operations; APVRS even created a 'Dennis Lam Lecture' in his name in 2023.
notes: Known professionally as Dennis S.C. Lam. Very public figure in ophthalmology (Power List Hall of Fame); Hurun lists wealth jointly with Li Xiaoting. Approachable via C-MER corporate office or ophthalmology conferences (APAO/APVRS). No published IR email found.
